text:
Exact

 Write an app once. It runs natively on the web, macOS, iOS, and Linux, and an AI
agent can build it, run it, see it, and test it on every one of them. 

Android and Windows are early and in progress: an app builds and runs on both, and
what each still lacks is under Not yet, or not at all.

 Building an app? With the tools installed (Quick start, step 1),
run bun scripts/exact.mjs setup once, make the app with bun scripts/exact.mjs new ,
and read docs/start-here.md (for a website,
 docs/start-here-site.md ): that guide is the only required
reading. The rest of this page describes Exact for people deciding whether to use it
or working on it.

 [!TIP]
 Try it with a coding agent. On a Mac with Xcode, Rust, Bun, and Chrome installed,
 give Claude Code this prompt:
 
 
 
 A fresh agent given the earlier version of this prompt on a clean clone (2026-10-04, Hermes already in the
 machine cache, Cargo's cache warm) finished in about 57 minutes, and its tests passed
 on all three platforms. About 25 of those minutes were the first macOS and iOS builds,
 roughly 13 minutes each; later builds take a minute or two. On a machine that has
 lacked Hermes, its source build came first and added time. Current setup downloads and
 verifies the pinned host/iOS bundles once instead; ordinary builds stay offline.

 
 
 Web 
 iOS 
 macOS 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The browser's own DOM and CSS 
 UIKit views, native controls and the system's tab bar 
 AppKit views and native controls 
 
 

 One app.contract , the same screen on three hosts, captured by the agent driver. Softwear is a demonstration store you can generate from exact-templates : it shows Alternative Apparel's catalog, is not affiliated with that brand, and takes no real orders or payments. 

Exact is a cross-platform application runtime. You describe your interface in
 Contract , a small declarative language, and you write your data logic in
 TypeScript or Rust ; a plain HTTP read needs neither, as it can be declared in
Contract. The Contract compiler turns the interface into a compact
 plan . On the web, that plan becomes one ES module over a 20 KB runtime that drives
the real DOM. On macOS, iOS, and Linux, a Rust runner executes the same plan, a Rust
layout kernel computes every box with CSS rules, and each platform draws with its own
tools: AppKit, UIKit, or a GPU painter. There is no webview and no JavaScript bridge
in the UI, and no app JavaScript runs before the first pixel.

 [!NOTE]
 Exact is pre-1.0 and changes daily. There is no API stability, no backwards
 compatibility, and no migration guide, by design ( rules/DEFERRED.md ). This
 repository, exact2 , is a rebuild of an earlier one ("exact1"), whose design
 documents are research, never authority.

The design record is a separate, private repository of numbered documents (LLPs),
 expo/exact-llp , which those with access clone into llp/ (git ignores it). This
README and the guides cite it by number ( LLP 1115 D7 ). The guides under docs/ 
are the public documentation.

To upgrade an inherited app, run these commands from its directory:

 

For the Snapback mutation refusal rewrite, see the
upgrade note in start-here.

 Contents

- Three principles
- How it works
- Quick start
- Contract
- Example apps
- What works today, and what doesn't yet
- Repository map
- Working on Exact

 Three principles

 1. Agent native

Exact assumes much of the code will be written by AI agents. An agent can make an app,
run it, look at it, operate it, and prove it works without a person in the loop.

- Ten operations, the same on every host. tree · screenshot · tap · type · state
 · layout · logs · clock · prefer · perf drive the web, macOS, iOS (Simulator or a real
 iPhone), and Linux through one script, scripts/agent.mjs . There are ten on purpose:
 the predecessor's agent API grew to eighty wire names, one reasonable addition at a
 time.
- The clock belongs to the agent. Between two operations nothing moves. Instead of
 sleeping until an animation finishes, the agent says clock +60000 or
 clock settle and reads the result. No timing flakes, no waits.
- Tests are scripts of those operations. An app.test.contract file runs unchanged
 on any host, with no second evaluator.
- Every tool speaks to machines. contract build --json gives diagnostics with
 stable ids and source ranges. contract symbols gives navigation. A development
 source map leads from any node on screen back to the line that declared it.
 The driver refuses to drive a build older than its sources and names the rebuild.
- Contract is small on purpose. A whole app fits in a context window. Every write
 is declared, every list is keyed, every value is typed. Mistakes are refusals that
 say what to do, not quiet misbehavior.

 

 2. Speed is king

Speed of the app and speed of the loop. Each budget in rules/RULES.md is tracked on
each hour, and a regression is a P0 with a name on it.

 Budget Target 
 --- --- 
 Cold start to interactive first frame 100 ms p50 
 Dev restart, edit to present 100 ms p50 
 App JavaScript executed before first pixel none 
 Touch one line, rebuild that crate 30 s 
 The blocking gate, warm after a one-crate edit 30 s 

How the design keeps those numbers:

- The boot path executes and compiles nothing. TypeScript is compiled to Hermes
 bytecode at build time and loads after the first pixel. The first frame comes from
 data baked into the plan.
- Pay only for what you use. GPU rendering, the Markdown editor, text flow, and
 browser SQLite are separate artifacts, loaded on demand. Nothing is a feature flag
 on a core crate.
- The web gets its own small runtime. On the RealWorld ("Conduit") benchmark,
 Exact's runtime was up about 300 ms before the React SSR build had hydrated. It used
 26 KB of code against React's 81 KB
 (LLP 1071).
- Edits land in about a tenth of a second. On a fresh app made by exact new , a
 saved Contract or TypeScript edit was rebuilt and in the page in 99 ms.

 3. Write the web, ship the platform

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
These steps were run on macOS on Apple Silicon. Linux also runs the web loop, the Linux host, and the iOS cross compiler. On Windows, use WSL 2 with Ubuntu 24.04 for iOS builds.

1. Install the tools

  • Rust through rustup. The pinned stable toolchain in rust-toolchain.toml installs itself the first time Cargo runs.

  • Bun 1.4.2, the version package.json pins. Node and npm are not needed.

  • Google Chrome. The agent drives the web through headless Chrome. Set CHROME to use another Chromium.

  • Xcode 27.1 or later, for Apple builds on macOS (exact setup --check checks it). For iOS builds on Linux/WSL, install Swift 6.4.2, xtool 1.24.0, LLVM 23, and apple-codesign 0.29.0. Download Xcode 27.1 from Apple, then run APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 xtool sdk install --slim /path/to/Xcode_27.1.xip on Linux. This extracts the SDK; it does not run Xcode. The environment variable lets xtool's AppImage run without FUSE. In WSL 2, keep the checkout and SDK in Ubuntu's Linux filesystem. Put LLVM's bin directory on PATH and set EXACT_APPLE_LLVM_BIN to that directory (on Ubuntu, /usr/lib/llvm-23/bin). Swift and rcodesign must also be on PATH; IPA archives also need zip. For a signed device archive, set EXACT_IDENTITY to an absolute PKCS#12 file path, EXACT_APPLE_SIGN_PASSWORD_FILE to its password file, and EXACT_PROFILE to the app’s provisioning profile. Set EXACT_PROFILE_DIR to a directory containing companion extension profiles. Profile decoding needs openssl. On macOS, EXACT_IDENTITY continues to name a Keychain identity. EXACT_APPLE_SDK can select a Darwin SDK bundle outside xtool's default ~/.swiftpm/swift-sdks/darwin.artifactbundle. Watch simulator companions require xtool sdk install /path/to/Xcode_27.1.xip without --slim, so Exact can install the retained watch SDK on the first watch build. Icon Composer projects retain their live SVG layers on iOS 26 and newer; Linux uses the manifest’s PNG icons entry as artwork for older iOS versions. The portable compiler supports the checked-in projects’ default SVG group and opaque sRGB background; other Composer settings are refused explicitly. For the SVG filter kernels and Canvas 2D GPU module on x86-64 Linux/WSL, install Wine 9 or newer and download Metal Developer Tools for Windows. Extract the installer with 7z x -o/path/to/metal-tools Metal_Developer_Tools6.2Windows.exe, then set EXACT_APPLE_METAL_TOOLS=/path/to/metal-tools (the directory containing bin/metal.exe). The qualified compiler is Metal 32023.850 from the 6.2 Windows installer. EXACT_APPLE_WINE can select Wine's executable; otherwise Exact uses Ubuntu's /usr/lib/wine/wine64 when present, then wine on PATH. Wine runs only at build time. Its prefix defaults to ~/.cache/exact/windows-metal; WINEPREFIX overrides it.

  • Hermes, only for TypeScript apps on native hosts. Exact consumes Ibex's pinned, attested 260318099.0.4 release bundle; ordinary Cargo builds are offline and never download or compile an engine. Install it once for each target before building (for this Mac, use aarch64-apple-darwin):

    cargo run --manifest-path vendor/ibex/crates/hermes-lean-sys-installer/Cargo.toml -- --target <triple>

    The installer verifies the bundle and publishes it under ~/.cargo/hermes-lean-sys/. The v4 set supports macOS, Linux, Windows, iOS devices and the universal iOS Simulator, plus tvOS devices and arm64 tvOS Simulators. Linux and Windows select Ibex's English intl tier; Apple keeps Hermes's OS-backed Intl. HERMES_LEAN_SYS_DIR is only an explicit development override, not normal setup.

To install the pinned Bun beside any existing installation: curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | BUN_INSTALL=~/.bun-1.4.2 bash -s bun-v1.4.2. Use ~/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun for the commands below if it is not on your PATH. bun scripts/exact.mjs setup installs the declared stable and web nightly Rust toolchains, their components/targets (the nightly's clippy lints a game's web bake), matching wasm-bindgen, pinned Binaryen and Bun dependencies, installs the pinned Hermes host bundle and the iOS/tvOS bundles this machine builds, and fetches the crates of exact2's lock and the game SDK's (game/app/shells.lock), since every bake resolves offline. It keeps Binaryen in ~/.cache/exact/binaryen; builds find it automatically. setup --check invokes Ibex's installer in its offline check mode for that same target set. The resolver authenticates the canonical receipts, archives, compiler and host/target HBC pairing without installing anything; its exit status and diagnostic are the check's result.

With the Linux cross SDK installed, setup also installs the iOS Rust targets. Build a simulator bundle with bun host/apple/build.mjs --ios --no-install hello-apple. In an app made with exact new, bun exact.mjs ios builds without installing on Linux/WSL; ios --prebuild runs the same build in the background. Linux defaults to an ARM64 simulator target; EXACT_IOS_SIM_ARCH=x86_64 selects an Intel simulator. Execution needs an iOS simulator on macOS or an iPhone; compilation, asset catalog generation, App Intents metadata and ad-hoc signing run on Linux.

Production builds with custom native views also validate the compiled factory roster. Linux can import a simulator qualification with EXACT_NATIVE_ROSTERS=/path/to/qualification.json. It contains { "version": 1, "probes": [{ "probeSha256": "…", "roster": "<JSON object>" }] }. The build writes native-probes.json beside its link products to identify the retained probe directory. Copy that whole directory to the Mac and run its ExactRosterProbe with xcrun simctl spawn <simulator> <directory>/ExactRosterProbe. Use the printed JSON as the qualification's roster string and the listed probeSha256 as its digest. The digest covers every file in the directory: the executable, module library, package libraries and declared frameworks. Changing any of them requires a new simulator run. Without a matching qualification, a production build refuses rather than accepting an absent factory or omitting its first-frame declaration. Development builds retain the existing manifest fallback.

2. Run Caltrain in the browser
git clone https://github.com/expo/exact.git
cd exact
bun scripts/exact.mjs setup
bun host/web/dev.mjs            # Caltrain, at http://127.0.0.1:8765/

The first run compiles the toolchain, which takes a few minutes. After that, open apps/caltrain/app.contract, change some text, and save. The page rebuilds and reloads in about a tenth of a second. Add --lan to open the same page from a phone on your network. The server answers only to the names it prints (a DNS-rebinding guard; any other Host gets 421); to share it through a tunnel such as tuft host, name the tunnel's host with --allow-host <name> (repeatable; name:port pins a port). An allowed name reaches the page and its reload stream, never the local installer's token.

3. Run it natively
bun host/apple/build.mjs --run              # macOS
bun host/apple/build.mjs --ios --run        # an iOS Simulator (--device --run for a connected iPhone)
cargo build --profile host-dev -p caltrain-linux   # Linux: a DRM/KMS console, or headless anywhere (--release to ship)

A first native build takes ten to fifteen minutes on a laptop; later builds reuse it and take a minute or two. Watch its output rather than waiting blind. iOS commands use an iPhone simulator that's already booted, or boot the newest iPhone Pro. To choose one, set EXACT_SIM to its name or UDID (or pass --sim to build.mjs), and keep the same setting for agent.mjs ios.

On Linux, a development build can serve its screen with EXACT_VNC=1 and EXACT_VNC_PASSWORD set to 1–8 bytes. It listens on 127.0.0.1:5900; an explicit EXACT_VNC=host:port selects another address. Production bakes ignore both variables.

4. Drive it the way an agent does
bun host/web/build.mjs caltrain-web         # the build the agent's web host serves
bun scripts/agent.mjs web tree "tap change-station" "type station-search Palo" state "screenshot out.png"
bun scripts/agent.mjs web --test apps/caltrain/app.test.contract

usage.title: Example apps
usage.html:
Each app lives in apps/<name>/. Run one on the web with bun host/web/dev.mjs --app <name>, on macOS with bun host/apple/build.mjs <name>-apple --run, and on iOS by adding --ios. All of these screenshots come from the web host, taken by scripts/agent.mjs.

To learn from, start with Shelf, the recipe app. It names no colour and no font size, and scripts/no-tells.mjs holds it to that, so it shows what an app that leaves presentation to the platform looks like on each host. Then read these four for what each teaches. They were written before LLP 1115 and paint their own colours and sizes, so take their structure, not their style:

App What it teaches
Caltrain A Rust data crate, authored tests, routes, an optional GPU module
Weatherlight TypeScript with fetch and grants
Fieldnotes Storage: SQLite, files, backup and restore
Recorder The microphone through @exact/media-capture and @exact/recording
Caltrain
The app that defines v1: nearby stations, live departure boards, search, theming, a Canvas 2D line map, and an aurora GPU sky. Rust data. Every host.		 Weatherlight
Weather from Open-Meteo under a GPU-animated sky that follows the hour you pick. TypeScript data and a wgpu module.		 Spark
A swipe deck: throw a card with your finger, and it flies off with your release velocity. Pan gestures and springs on every host.		 Expose
A pretend phone OS (lock screen, home, Messages with an AI assistant, Reader) set in custom fonts. TypeScript. The assistant needs an OpenRouter key.
Calendar
Month pages, draggable sheets, events dragged between days, wallpaper themes, SQLite. It lives outside apps/, so set EXACT_APP_DIR to run it.		 Sparkline
A market list of animated SVG charts that draw in and pulse.		 Photo Editor
Rotate, pan, and crop, through a native module.		 Video Player
A bundled clip that shrinks out of the way when the keyboard opens.
Exact Live
A creative-production workspace: a photo grid you reorder by dragging, a crew chat that can take a 10,000-message burst, and a Markdown runbook. Rust data.		 Still (Interaction Gallery)
Drag to reorder, pan and zoom photos, a resizable sheet with a nested list, and 100 to 25,000 records.
Reflow
Seven typography studies after Cheng Lou's Pretext demos: text flowing around moving balls, a dragon, masonry, and a magazine spread. Line heights come from font metrics read at build time.		 Textflow
Text around shapes with CSS's shape-outside and wrap-flow: draggable orbs, a dancer, an editorial layout. One Rust walker shared by every host.
Markdown
A Markdown reader that opens files from Finder or the command line (mdview README.md). Its sibling LLP (llpview) reads a directory of numbered design documents (LLPs).		 Conduit (RealWorld)
The RealWorld Medium clone against its hosted API. It's the benchmark that compared Exact's web build with React 19. Web only.
SVG Gallery: SVG as the browser renders it, one page per feature, held to Chrome's pixels on every host.
Canvas Gallery: the HTML Canvas 2D API drawn by the browser, Core Graphics, or tiny-skia, and compared to Chrome.
More apps, labs, and stress tests
App What it shows Notes
Fieldnotes A local notebook with pins, search, SQLite storage, and JSON backup and restore TypeScript + Rust
Messages A port of Expo's chat demo, talking to models through OpenRouter Needs bun apps/messages/service.ts and an OpenRouter key
Type Tour Phone-OS screens as a type specimen for the Expose fonts No JavaScript at all
Map Demo Native modules: MapKit on Apple and OpenStreetMap on the web
Carousel A horizontal virtualized list of 25,000 cards
Motion Gallery Animated GIF and WebP images and CSS keyframes, compared across hosts
Update Lab Live replacement of Contract, TypeScript, and Rust in a running app Hand-testing lab
Messages Stress, Completion Storm, Markdown Stress 100k-message histories, 128 parallel requests, and 4 MiB documents, under load Opt-in workloads (LLP 1041)
Native Fixture, Auth Fixture The native-module interface; OAuth with PAR, DPoP, and PKCE against a local server Test fixtures
Beacons, Tennis, … Games on the optional engine add-on: Rust gameplay, Contract menus bun game/dev.mjs beacons
